finish.notes: Architect-spec premium finish. Maximum quality. Complete system approach.

coverage_profiles.notes: Primed smooth trim surfaces. Uses PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF paint coverage. Coverage varies by profile complexity — complex profiles have more surface area per LF, lowering effective coverage. Standard (ogee/cove) profile assumed for base rate.
assumptions: Standard profile complexity (1.0x). Adjust for Simple (0.85x surface area = higher coverage) through Ornate (1.40x surface area = lower coverage)
Two-coat system. Third coat at QT5 brush/roll has same per-coat coverage.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Between-coat sanding — spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 — spot sand nibs and rough spots only

consumables.notes: Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD 15.4.1). Flexible sponges conform to defects instead of removing them.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.usage: Between-coat sanding — thorough full sand at QT5
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required. Rigid sanding block mandatory (FFD 15.4.1).

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects. Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for between-coat sanding (FFD 15.4.1). One block per crew, reusable across coats.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush application tool for trim finish. Also used for touch-up with spray method.
consumables.notes: One per painter per material change. 2-2.5" standard for trim. Quality brush essential for smooth finish — do not skimp at higher QTs.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for trim spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for trim work. Tip life extends across many LF of trim.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~200 LF of trim. Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Touch-up cracked joints in initial prep (post-primer-cure)
consumables.notes: Touch-up only — full caulk job was completed during prime spec (SF_TRIM_NC_PRIME). Approximately 10-15% of joints may need re-caulk after primer cure.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle
consumables.usage: Touch-up fill revealed defects in initial prep
consumables.notes: Touch-up only — heavy fill was completed during prime spec. Spot fill defects revealed after primer cure.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Wall masking at trim edge (spray method, or any method when walls are SS_PAINTED_*)
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Used for wall_adjacent zone masking and fixture covers.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12")
consumables.usage: Wall masking adjacent to trim during spray or when walls are SS_PAINTED_*
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. 12" width covers wall adjacent to trim. Also needed for brush when walls are SS_PAINTED_* — per RC-007.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth runner
consumables.usage: Floor protection along trim perimeter (baseboard work area)
consumables.notes: Runner-style drops along trim work area for drip catching. 1-2 per painter, reusable. Required when floor_type = finished or partial.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners along trim work area perimeter
floor_perimeter.notes: Perimeter drops along baseboard and trim run areas. Not needed on subfloor.

wall_adjacent.notes: Required for spray to protect wall from overspray. Also required for brush when walls are SS_PAINTED_* (RC-007) — tape line only, no paper needed for brush.

fixture_covers.notes: Tape over nearby outlets and switches when spraying trim.

Shadow box / picture frame molding linear footage
Trim joint LF for touch-up caulking scope
Floor protection area along trim perimeter
Wall masking LF at trim edge
required_inputs.condition: application_method = spray, or walls are SS_PAINTED_*

compatibility_rules.description: All three finish systems are compatible with field-applied primer (SS_PRIMED_FIELD)
compatibility_rules.notes: Light sand primer surface for mechanical adhesion before finish application.

compatibility_rules.description: All three finish systems are compatible with factory primer (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY)
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. Verify primer integrity if exposed to weather during construction.

risk_notes.risk: Overworking Advance or Emerald Urethane causes roping, brush marks, or orange peel
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Sand marks out between coats with rigid block. Build finish through multiple sanded coats.

risk_notes.risk: Different film thickness or sanding patterns across trim types within same room
risk_notes.mitigation: Consistent mil thickness across all trim. Box materials from same batch. Full coat over any spot repairs.

risk_notes.topic: Gloss finish at QT5 magnifies imperfections
risk_notes.risk: Every brush mark, dust nib, and sanding scratch shows in gloss finish
risk_notes.mitigation: 3+ coats with thorough 220-320 grit sanding between each. Meticulous dust cleanup. Controlled environment. Rigid sanding block mandatory.

risk_notes.topic: Temperature affects working time and leveling
risk_notes.risk: Cold conditions slow drying but may improve open time. Hot conditions accelerate drying, further shortening already-short working times.
risk_notes.mitigation: Monitor ambient temperature. Ensure within product PDS range (generally 50-90°F). Adjust application pace accordingly.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection is recommended by quality tier per Fine Finish Doctrine Section 3: QT3=SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4=SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5=SYS_FF_PREMIUM. These are recommendations — contractor retains discretion on product selection (RC-005). System identifies proper application characteristics for each product category.
material_notes.finish_only_scope: This is a finish-only spec. No primer products are included — primer is handled by companion SF_TRIM_NC_PRIME. Input state is SS_PRIMED_FIELD or SS_PRIMED_FACTORY.
material_notes.coverage_note: Coverage uses PDCA standard: 1 LF trim = 1 SF coverage area for standard profile. Complex profiles have more surface area per LF — apply profile_complexity modifier to coverage calculation.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is a waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel — NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Both have short working times and dry fast.
material_notes.open_time: Both Advance and Emerald Urethane have short working times — fast dry is a production benefit but demands proper first-pass technique. Do not attempt to rework after application (FFD 15.3.1).

assumptions.value: 350-450 LF/gal for standard profile trim on primed surface
assumptions.note: Based on PDCA 1 LF = 1 SF standard. Varies by profile complexity.

assumptions.value: 10-15% of joints need re-caulk after primer cure
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines post-primer-cure joint failure rate. Estimated from field experience.
